THE THINKING↙
01

Give the workspace room.

The remote display fills the space beneath the session header. No input rail, dock or touch overlay occupies the desktop workspace.

02

Same visual language.

Paper surfaces, olive accents and a compact session header carry the mobile reference into a desktop workspace. Use your physical keyboard and mouse.

03

Keep session actions close.

Fit, full viewport and session settings remain in the header. Mobile browsers keep their touch controls in the production client.

↳ A deliberate detail

Click the simulated editor and type with your keyboard. Session state is always labeled; this prototype never connects to a host.
